candidates.reason: The exact-timestamped v1 preprint is fresh, non-duplicate and technically consequential. It supports a practical configuration-level evaluation decision with independently produced benchmark context while retaining the unreproduced-preprint boundary.
The verified DevDay keynote event crossed the mandatory 48-hour publication boundary before selection; a later retrieval or recap cannot replace the launch event.

Index Us already covers HydraFusion routing. An additional editor surface and administrator preview controls do not materially change the existing deployment decision or earn a separate long-form article.
The paper was nearing the freshness boundary and overlapped recent Index Us agent-control coverage. It was weaker than the selected fresh evaluation story.

decision.reason: cua-speedrun supplies fresh, exact-timestamped evidence that desktop timing, reasoning and harness choices can materially change success, task time and cost. The article turns the paper's narrow findings and independent benchmark context into a configuration-level deployment test without claiming peer review, reproduction or hands-on Index Us testing.

claims.text: The cua-speedrun v1 preprint was submitted at 2026-09-30T17:48:06Z.
The project standardises a virtual-machine setup, execution pipeline and common agent interface across OSWorld, OSWorld2, CUA-World and MyPCBench.
The paper reports mean verifier score, mean task time and mean model cost per task for complete configurations.
Task timing begins when the instruction reaches the agent and excludes provisioning, setup, initialisation and verification.
The v1 evaluation uses 50 of 295 OSWorld tasks and 52 of 63 OSWorld2 tasks, with 56 and 21 agent configurations respectively.

In one five-seed GPT-6 Astra low-effort comparison, fast I/O reduced mean environment processing from 12.68 seconds to 0.34 seconds per task while total mean task time rose from 89.5 seconds to 99.0 seconds.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 section 3.2, Figure 5 and Appendices B and F.

claims.text: The paper's authors attribute the fast-I/O slowdown to early screenshots, extra interaction and waits.

For Gemini 3 Flash Preview on OSWorld, moving from low to medium reasoning changed mean score from 33.6 to 57.6 per cent and mean task time from 492 to 268 seconds, while generated tokens per task increased.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 section 3.2, Figure 3 and Appendix E.

claims.text: Changing the agent harness altered both task score and time for the same model and reasoning setting, and neither tested harness was uniformly better.
OSWorld-Human reported that model calls accounted for most latency and that its 16 evaluated agents used 2.7-4.3 times more steps than the human-derived trajectories.
The original OSWorld paper describes 369 tasks spanning real web and desktop applications, file operations and multi-application workflows.
OSWorld 2.0 reports 20.6 per cent binary completion and a 54.8 per cent partial score for its strongest tested configuration under the primary 500-step setting.
A model name alone is not an adequate procurement or evaluation unit for a computer-use agent.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises are the measured changes under harness, reasoning and environment timing variations in s2; the article presents this as an operational conclusion.

claims.text: Teams should version the complete configuration and measure accepted completion, end-to-end elapsed time, cost and review or recovery work on their own workload.
claims.sourceLocator: The recommendation is original synthesis grounded in the timing boundary, loop length, run variation and binary-versus-partial distinction.

claims.text: Success, task time and model cost do not establish safety, permission compliance, ambiguity handling or absence of harmful side effects.
claims.sourceLocator: This is a scope boundary derived from the paper's defined metrics, not an allegation that a tested system was unsafe.
